newsitem.title: GERMANY: MG shares jump on positive profit report.
newsitem.headline: MG shares jump on positive profit report.

text.p: Shares in German metals and trading company Metallgesellschaft jumped on Tuesday after the firm said it had reached its goals for the 1995-1996 financial year and would definitely surpass last year's profits.
MG stocks hit 28.58 marks ($18.73) in early trade, gaining 1.22 marks or over four percent and then came back to 28.35 marks.
"We can now say that we have done extraordinarily well in a difficult area," management board chairman Kajo Neukirchen said in MG's internal newspaper.
In May, the company said it was sticking to a pretax profit goal of 300 million marks for the 1995/1996 year to September 30, despite the impact of the weak economy on its business.
In the 1994/1995 financial year MG made 171 million marks pretax profit.
Neukirchen said the quick turnaround in results was not just temporary but the starting point of a long-term climb in the worth of the company.
He said he hoped the statement would be a positive surprise for the stock market.
"We're doing well in all areas and we have met the requirements for a successful 1996/1997 financial year," he said.
Metallgesellschaft has undergone a complete restructuring since it ran into billions of marks of losses over risky U.S. oil deals late in 1993. ($ = 1.525 German Marks)
